card.name: Words introducing a trial or analysis
card.fires_on: Short words right before a study or trial is described, such as "a" in "In a pooled analysis" or "marketing" in "premarketing clinical study". Seen in label sections on adverse reactions and trial results.

modes.label: Article opening a study
modes.description: "a", "A", "this" or "One" starting a sentence or clause that introduces a trial or finding.
modes.example: In<< a>> pooled analysis of 7 placebo controlled trials

modes.label: Modifier before study noun
modes.description: An adjective or prefix-like word that sits just before "clinical study" or "analysis".
modes.example: During a pre<<marketing>> clinical study with an immediate-release centan

modes.label: Evaluation verb
modes.description: A verb such as "evaluated" after "not been systematically" in a statement about study coverage.
modes.example: escitalopram oxalate has not been systematically<< evaluated>> in patients with a seizure disorder

card.writes: Suppresses "data" tokens, so it seems to steer away from the word data right after these study-introducing words.
card.plain: It marks the small word just before a trial or analysis is named, and it discourages the word "data" there.
